name: autognome
skin_color: Polished brass, ironwood, or burnished copper
special_features: Articulated brows, gemstone eyes, clockwork construction
lore:
To the uninitiated, an Autognome might appear merely as a complex clockwork toy. Yet, these three-foot-tall marvels are far more. Constructed from polished brass, ironwood, and burnished copper, their forms mirror the diminutive stature of their creators. Their faces are remarkably expressive, featuring articulated brows and gemstone eyes that pulse with a soft, internal luminescence. Each is a unique masterpiece, bearing the aesthetic flourishes—and perhaps the eccentricities—of the specific tinkerer who forged them.

Their origins lie within the soot-stained laboratories of the Rock Gnomes. Originally conceived as tireless assistants or companions for lonely inventors, Autognomes are imbued with a "spark of sentience"—a sophisticated blend of intricate mechanical logic and a dash of arcane lightning. They are the living legacy of a creator’s genius, designed to endure long after the mortal gnomes who tightened their first bolts have returned to the earth.

Culturally, Autognomes are defined by a profound sense of purpose. While they lack biological drives like hunger, they possess an insatiable curiosity and a deeply ingrained sense of loyalty. Many spend centuries perfecting a single craft or guarding the ancestral halls of their makers. Others, finding themselves "masterless" after their creator’s passing, wander the world in search of a new directive. They often adopt the whimsical mannerisms and joyous outlook of gnomish society, celebrating existence through the meticulous maintenance of their gears and the pursuit of knowledge. To an Autognome, life is not a biological accident, but a grand experiment in which they are both the scientist and the subject.
